text: With no cars and no factories, the air is cleaner than it has been in more than a century.
Grass pushes up through every crack in the pavement. Each winter, water freezes inside those cracks, and splits them a little wider.
Deer wander down streets that were built for cars.
Foxes raise their young under porches. Birds nest behind broken windows.
In the supermarkets, almost every scrap of food has rotted, or been eaten by rats and insects.
Gutters fill with leaves. Rain gets in. Wooden roofs begin to rot, and sag.
Young trees are already taller than the cars they grow between.
But the biggest change is still to come.
